title: HighLevel API Documentation
snippet:
## **API Access Across HighLevel Plans**
HighLevel provides API access across all subscription plans, including Starter, Unlimited, and Agency Pro.
Both **OAuth 2.0** and **Private Integration Tokens (PIT)** are available across all plans, allowing developers to build integrations and access supported APIs without requiring an Agency Pro subscription.
API Availability
| API capability | Starter ($97) | Unlimited ($297) | Agency Pro ($497) |
|---|---|---|---|
| OAuth 2.0 authentication | Available | Available | Available |
| Private Integration Tokens (PIT) | Available | Available | Available |
| Standard API endpoints | Available | Available | Available |
| Agency Pro-restricted endpoints | Not available | Not available | Available |
**Agency Pro-Restricted Endpoints**
While standard API access is available across all plans, certain endpoints require an Agency Pro ($497/month) subscription.
The following endpoints are currently documented as requiring Agency Pro:
| Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [Create Sub-Account](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/locations/create-location) | Create a new sub-account programmatically. |
| [Enable SaaS for Sub-Account](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/ghl/saas-api/enable-saas-location) | Enable SaaS functionality for a sub-account. |
**Note:** Additional endpoint-specific restrictions may apply. Refer to the [official HighLevel API documentation](https://marketplace.gohighlevel.com/docs/) for the latest requirements and supported API versions.
**Important Notes**
- OAuth 2.0 and PIT availability is not restricted by subscription tier.
- Access to individual endpoints depends on the required permissions, scopes, and applicable plan restrictions.
- Agency Pro is required only for endpoints or capabilities explicitly restricted to that plan.

**Q. Is API access available on all HighLevel plans?**
API access varies by plan:
- Starter & Unlimited: Basic API access
- Founder Plan: Advanced API access, including OAuth and agency-level tokens
Some endpoints may only be available on higher plans.

title: Creating Sub-Accounts using Zapier
snippet:
**Important:** Creating sub-accounts through the API requires the **Founder Plan ($497/month)**, formerly Agency Pro, which includes Advanced API Access.

Before getting started, ensure you have:
- An active HighLevel Founder Plan subscription.
- Agency-level access to HighLevel.
- A Zapier plan that supports Webhooks.
- An agency-level Private Integration Token (PIT) or OAuth 2.0 authorization.
- The `locations.write` API scope.
- A form, workflow, or other event to trigger sub-account creation.

**Q: Which HighLevel plan is required to create sub-accounts using APIs?**
The Founder Plan ($497/month), formerly Agency Pro, includes the advanced API access required for programmatic sub-account creation.

title: GoHighLevel API: Keys, Plans, Limits and How to Connect
snippet:
GoHighLevel's help center says Starter and Unlimited get basic API access, and Agency Pro gets advanced access. For a one-account tool, make a Private Integration token in Settings and send it as a Bearer token with a Version header. For an app many accounts install, use OAuth 2.0. Limits: 100 requests per 10 seconds and 200,000 a day.

All three plans have some API access, but only Agency Pro has the advanced kind. Here is what GoHighLevel's pricing page and its help article said on 18 October 2026:
| Plan | Price | Pricing page says | Help article says |
|---|---|---|---|
| Starter | $97 a month or $970 a year | No API line in the plan card | Basic API access |
| Unlimited | $297 a month or $2,970 a year | "Basic API Access" | Basic API access |
| Agency Pro | $497 a month or $4,970 a year | "Advanced API Access" | Advanced API access |
| Enterprise | No price listed | "Increase API Limit by request" | Not covered |

What is the difference? The help article says advanced access adds agency-level keys and "the upcoming OAuth 2.0 endpoints". Lower plans get location-level keys only, which means one sub-account at a time. It also says some endpoints may need a higher plan.
